title: Year 9 Science Test 1
topics: Variation and inheritance · Adaptation and extinction · Cells and the microscope · Atoms and the periodic table
instructions: You have 40 minutes. Answer all the questions.
Write your answers in the spaces on this paper. If you need more space, use the back of the page and write the question number.
The marks for each part are shown in brackets, for example [2]. There are 40 marks in total.
Read each question carefully. Use the science key words in your answers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Put one tick in each row to show whether the factor is abiotic (non-living) or biotic (living).
parts.answer: temperature: abiotic; predation: biotic; amount of light: abiotic; infectious disease: biotic. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A scar is caused by a cut. Complete the sentence.
gaps: A scar is an example of ______________________ variation.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Put one tick in each row to show whether the variation is continuous or discontinuous.
parts.answer: height: continuous; blood group: discontinuous; hand span: continuous; tongue rolling: discontinuous. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Some students measured the length of 40 leaves and drew a bar chart of their results. Should the bars touch each other? Tick one box and give a reason.
mcq: No, there should be gaps between the bars.
parts.answer: Yes (1). Leaf length is continuous variation / the lengths were put into groups that run on from each other, so there are no gaps (1).

parts.label: e
parts.text: What is a species?
parts.answer: A group of organisms that can breed together to produce offspring that can also breed (accept: organisms that can breed together to make fertile offspring).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the sentences using words from the box. Use each word once. One word is not needed.
gaps: Genetic information is stored in the ______________________ of a cell.
A sperm cell and an egg cell are both ______________________.
The new cell that is made is called a ______________________.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Tick the two characteristics that are inherited.
parts.answer: natural eye colour (1) and blood group (1). If more than two boxes are ticked, take one mark off for each extra tick, to a minimum of 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Brothers and sisters have the same parents, but they are not identical. Explain why.
parts.answer: Each gamete (sperm or egg) carries a different mixture of the parent's genetic information (1), so each child gets a different combination of genes from the two parents (1). Accept: they inherit different genes from each parent.

parts.label: a
parts.text: What is an adaptation?
parts.answer: A characteristic (feature) that helps an organism survive in its habitat.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A sand cat lives in the desert. Its fur is the same colour as the sand. Explain how this helps the sand cat to survive.
parts.answer: The fur is camouflage: the cat is hard to see against the sand (1), so it can creep up on prey / is not seen by predators, and so catches more food or is not eaten (1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Grey squirrels were brought to the UK from the USA. Red squirrels are now rare in most of the UK. Give two reasons why grey squirrels have replaced red squirrels.
parts.answer: Any two of: greys can eat unripe acorns, so they eat the food before the reds do (compete better for food); greys store more body fat, so more survive the winter; greys carry squirrel pox, a disease that kills reds.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Draw one line from each way of protecting a species to how it works.

right: endangered animals are bred in captivity to increase their numbers
seeds, gametes or cells are stored at a low temperature
an area where the habitat and the species living in it are protected

parts.answer: nature reserve: an area where the habitat and the species living in it are protected (1); breeding programme: endangered animals are bred in captivity (1); gene bank: seeds, gametes or cells stored at a low temperature (1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows a plant cell. Write the name of each labelled part.
parts.answer: A cell wall (1), B nucleus (1), C chloroplast (1), D vacuole (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which part of a cell controls what goes into and out of the cell? Tick one box.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A microscope has a x10 eyepiece lens and a x4 objective lens. Calculate the total magnification.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Give two rules for a good scientific drawing of cells.
parts.answer: Any two of: use a sharp pencil; make the drawing large; use clear single lines with no shading or colouring; draw only what you see; draw label lines with a ruler so they do not cross and end on the part; add a title with the magnification.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the table about the three particles in an atom. The first row has been done for you.
parts.answer: neutron: 0 (1), in the nucleus (1). electron: -1 (1), in shells around the nucleus (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: A sodium atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23.

sub.text: How many protons does the atom have?
How many neutrons does the atom have?

parts.label: c
parts.text: A sodium atom has 11 electrons. Complete its electron configuration.

parts.label: d
parts.text: A magnesium atom has atomic number 12. Write its electron configuration.
